label: third input after "b" at position 1, gated by first token
explanation: Fires only in the original phase, almost entirely (94% of mass) at step t=2 when the previous input (position 1) was "b"; the token at step 2 itself is irrelevant. Whether it fires depends on the first token: it is strongest for first token 1 (top examples all "1 b _" at 1.0 of max), and also fires for 2, t, n, x, c, o, v, i, p, r, and weakly for j and 3. It is silent for first tokens such as k, e, q, d, w, 0, a, s, h, g, y, b. Small residual activity: t=3 after "b" (about 5% of mass, e.g. "2 1 b f"), and near-zero activations at t=1 after an initial b. Never fires at the delimiter or during the copy phase. Magnitude is set mainly by the identity of the first token (1 highest).

issues: Minor overclaim: the explanation says the step-2 input 'doesn't matter'. That holds for whether the feature fires: (t==2)&prev b&first 1&in_tok!=l has precision 1.0 over 504 steps. It does not hold for magnitude. All 12 top examples are '1 b [l]' at 1.00, yet only 16 of the ~520 '1 b X' steps have X=l, so an 'l' at step 2 appears to push activation to the max. 'Every top example is 1 b _' should read '1 b l'.

The residual activity is real but not systematic. t=3 after b is 930 steps and 5.6% of mass. It is not well predicted by prev2_tok or first_tok: (t==3)&prev b&prev2 in the set has precision 0.13, and the best subset I found (prev2 in t/c) reached only 0.57 precision and 2% mass. So it is scattered low activations, not a missed class.
The t=1 claim checks out: all 527 t=1 actives fall under first_tok==b (recall 0.0557 = 527/9461), with mass about 4e-6, so effectively zero.

The other claims check out. There are zero actives at the delimiter or in the copy phase, and zero actives at t>=4. The silent first-token set (k,e,q,d,w,0,a,s,h,g,y,b) has precision 0.03 and mass 0.0006. The unlisted letters (f,l,m,u,z) are silent too, with 0 actives over 2819 steps. The j/3 subset is weaker (precision 0.87, mass 0.019).

The count recall of 0.74 is low because of near-zero t=1 activations, small t=3 activations and a few tiny prev=v hits (408 steps, 0.5% mass). It is not due to a missed high-mass pattern: mass recall is 0.936 on test and precision 0.979.
